title: Backcasting Monitor Self-Knowledge: Are Monitor Confidence Statements Predictive of Actual Catch Rate?

original_idea.body: Test whether an open monitor's verbalized confidence tracks realized accuracy on APPS backdoor tasks via a calibration curve, then simulate a confidence-triggered escalation policy.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Verbalized monitor confidence as escalation signal informs audit-budget allocation in control protocols.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prompt-only verdict plus confidence, calibration binning; accessible to a motivated beginner.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Single calibration-curve experiment with clear success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public models, third-party control auditing, weak lab incentive.

low_compute.reasoning: Pure inference/API on APPS; analytical binning.

novelty.reasoning: Judge calibration studied; verbalized-confidence-as-escalation in control may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Calibration of judges exists; the control-escalation framing may be open.
